lines: I.  Introduction

A design buys observations to certify the Top-k of a set of relations ranked by CAPACITY — the range max_a θ_ra − min_a θ_ra. Certifying means excluding every alternative that would change the answer, so the design's value is the cheapest such alternative.

Three quantities must be kept distinct. J_scalar is the pair-flip value computed at the CURRENT extrema with ordering constraints dropped; J_old is the quadratic programme inside the current-extrema region; J_full is the infimum over the whole alternative set, with the extrema free in either relation. and there is NO general order between J_scalar and J_full. Allocators are routinely built on J_scalar because it is cheap. This work asks what that costs when the extrema can move — and the answer is that it costs everything, in both directions.
II.  Contributions

C1.  THE SCALAR PROXY IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BY NO CONSTANT. Two explicit two-relation, three-action families drive J_full/J_scalar to 0 and to +∞. Both are exact-arithmetic constructions with explicit feasible alternatives — no optimiser, no sampled world, no seed — so no constant correction can repair the proxy. C2.  THE TRUE ALTERNATIVE SET IS A FINITE UNION OF CONVEX PAIR REGIONS, proved on the real RANGE target rather than a Top-1 surrogate, with the extrema chosen from the ALTERNATIVE and never frozen at truth, and no definiteness assumed anywhere. C3.  THE ENERGY ORACLE BECOMES A FINITE CHECK. A number lower-bounds the energy over the whole set iff it does so on every pair region, so no infimum over an infinite-dimensional set is ever taken. C4.  SHRINK AND EXPAND, AS EQUIVALENCES. Range ≤ z iff all cells lie in a common interval of length z; range ≥ z iff some ORDERED pair is separated by z. Equivalences, so nothing is relaxed. C5.  AN OPTIMALITY CERTIFICATE THAT NEEDS NO MATRIX INVERSE. The textbook dual requires M invertible. We prove optimality from primal feasibility, dual non-negativity, stationarity and complementary slackness using only symmetry and positive SEMIdefiniteness, so a singular information matrix costs no extra hypothesis and no pseudoinverse. C6.  THE SETUP-COST LAW, WITH INFEASIBILITY REPORTED AS INFEASIBILITY. An infeasible configuration has NO value and is never clamped to a small positive one; the crossing budget between two supports is derived, and when the two values are only bracketed we prove both orders remain consistent, so the honest output is UNDECIDED.

IV.  Results

THE TWO FAMILIES SEPARATE WITHOUT LIMIT. As η → 0 one family drives the ratio to zero and the other to infinity — PROVED bounds in exact arithmetic, not sampled points. ON RANDOM INSTANCES THE FAILURE IS PREDICTABLE. Over 6000 drawn instances, all 1367 on which the proxy overstates have a moving extremum, and none with fixed extrema does. ON THE MAIN PANEL, C_lucb IS THE BASELINE TO BEAT: 797 worlds certified at median 20,996 queries against 749 and 605. A result on this panel, not a domination theorem.

V.  Discussion

The families settle a methodological question rather than a numerical one. Because the proxy errs in both directions without a constant, no calibration of it is safe: an allocator trusting it may waste budget excluding an alternative that is already cheap, or stop early against one far cheaper than it believes. The correct object is the union of pair regions, and it is no harder to certify. Step 6 matters for practice as much as rigour: information matrices at sparse allocations are routinely singular, and a certificate surviving that without a pseudoinverse is what makes the oracle usable at the boundary. SCOPE. The DECOMPOSITION step is not formalised and the full oracle equality is not assembled. Free response table, known variance, positive precision. The certificate is SUFFICIENCY, not a characterisation. Only weak duality is proved — a search over 1054 instances found no gap, which is not a proof. No allocator built on this oracle has been compared against C_lucb.
VI.  Conclusions

When the extrema can move, the scalar pair-flip proxy is a bound in neither direction, and no constant repairs it. The true alternative set is a finite union of convex pair regions on the real range target; its energy oracle is a finite conjunction of convex problems; the inner problem has a closed form; and its certificate needs no matrix inverse, so a singular information matrix costs nothing extra. EXPERIMENT SCALE. The confirmatory panel is 10 seeds x 1,000 instances x 8 policies = 80,000 policy runs at horizon 131,072, drawing 5,042,978,194 samples in total, with 29.1% of runs censored at the horizon. That is ten times the earlier panel, and it ran as ten parallel processes for roughly six CPU-hours each. Every number reported on this poster comes from that run or from exact arithmetic; none is simulated for illustration.
